citation: Pillon NJ, Gabriel BM, Dollet L, Smith JAB, Sardon Puig L, et al. (2019). Transcriptomic profiling of skeletal muscle adaptations to exercise and inactivity. Nature Communications 11:470. (Singapore Sarcopenia Study cohort).
differential_method: limma-voom on RNA-seq counts (paper Supplementary Data 4, 'Sarcopenia' sheet)
original_threshold: FDR < 0.10 (per publication; n=40 underpowered for genome-wide padj < 0.05)

consensus_thresholds.rationale: Pillon n=40 has min padj=0.0796; using paper's published FDR<0.10 cutoff

table_provenance: Extracted by backend/scripts/extract_pillon_deg.py from Nat Comm Supplementary Data 4 (MOESM4_ESM.xlsx, 'Sarcopenia' sheet). Original archived as pillon_2019_SuppData4_full.xlsx. Fetched 2026-05-05.
table_columns: gene_symbol (from symbol.org.Hs.eg), log2fc (from coef_sarc), padj (from adjp_sarc), pvalue (from pval_sarc), ensembl_id
design_note: DISEASE-PROXY DESIGN, not young-vs-old. Sarcopenia = accelerated/advanced muscle aging. Concordance with healthy aging datasets validates rejuvenation signal.
limitations: All-male cohort; eliminates sex confound but limits generalizability to female aging.
role_in_consensus: Independent secondary signal — sarcopenia as advanced-aging proxy. Genes up in sarcopenia AND up in healthy aging (GSE164471/GTEx) are the highest-confidence aged-enriched markers.
